dedupe_keys.name: oemetadata open energy metadata standard json schema json ld context template and examples

description: Open Energy Metadata (OEMetadata) is a metadata standard for energy data, used to describe datasets from energy system models so they are findable and reusable. It is maintained by the Open Energy Platform community with the Reiner Lemoine Institut and is the metadata format of the Open Energy Platform database. Coverage: generic, applied mainly to European energy system modelling data. The standard extends the Frictionless Data Package specification with energy-specific keys in a nested JSON structure: context and funding, spatial and temporal coverage and resolution, sources, licences with attribution, contributors, review status and resource schemas down to field units, with a JSON-LD context mapping keys to Open Energy Ontology terms. Format and access: a JSON schema, context, empty template, example and key descriptions for each version, published on GitHub, as a Python package and with MkDocs documentation; free. Licence: MIT. Caveats: it is a schema, not data, versions differ in structure (version 2 reorganised the keys), and adoption outside the openmod community is limited. Simulation uses: documenting input and result datasets of energy capacity planning and optimisation models so they can be exchanged and compared. Related records: the Open Energy Platform (data-open-energy-platform) stores data described with OEMetadata, and GENeSYS-MOD (model-genesys-mod) is one of the model frameworks documented there.
